Gluttonous

GLUT-uh-nus · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Gluttonous is excessively greedy in eating or drinking.

The gluttonous puppy ate its own dinner, then finished the cat's food before anyone noticed.

Worked Example

At the buffet, the gluttonous diner returned for a fifth plate before most guests had finished their first.

Gluttonous describes excessive, often uncontrolled eating or consumption, usually with a disapproving tone.

How Gluttonous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

greedy

greedy: having excessive desire for food or wealth

ravenous

ravenous: extremely hungry, eager to eat

Antonyms

abstemious

abstemious: moderate in eating and drinking

moderate

moderate: not excessive or extreme

How Strong Is It? — hungry → gluttonous → ravenous

hungry vs. gluttonous

hungry vs. gluttonous: Hungry simply describes wanting food; gluttonous implies eating far past the point of need, to excess.

ravenous vs. gluttonous

ravenous vs. gluttonous: Ravenous describes intense hunger in the moment, while gluttonous describes a habitual pattern of excessive eating.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — glutt

root — glutt: to swallow (Latin (gluttire))

suffix — -onous

suffix — -onous: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: glutt- ('to swallow') + -onous together describe someone who swallows food excessively.

Use the root in a new word: glutton

Use the root in a new word: glutton: Glutton is the noun form of the same word family, naming the excessively greedy eater directly.
